blogs.title: Not Just T1 or T2: When to Suspect MODY in Young Adults
blogs.description: A discussion on the 'diagnostic dilemma' of early-onset diabetes. This post will focus on the clinical red flags for Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY), including strong family history, the lack of autoimmune markers, and why relying on BMI or 'metabolic syndrome' features is increasingly unreliable for distinguishing MODY from Type 2 Diabetes in modern populations.

blogs.title: The SGLT2 Trap: Why Standard T2D Therapy Can Be Dangerous in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: An analysis of the unique renal pathophysiology of HNF1A-MODY. This post explores how HNF1A mutations naturally reduce SGLT2 expression, explaining why adding a pharmacological SGLT2 inhibitor can lead to a precarious 'double-hit' effect, increasing the risk of severe dehydration, vascular collapse, and paradoxical diabetic ketoacidosis.

blogs.title: Precision Prescribing: Moving Beyond Insulin in Monogenic Diabetes
blogs.description: A look at the therapeutic pivot that occurs after a genetic diagnosis. This post examines the rationale for discontinuing insulin in HNF1A-MODY and the evidence for using low-dose sulfonylureas or GLP-1 receptor agonists to manage glycemic control while preserving residual $\beta$-cell function.

blogs.title: Decoding the Labs: C-Peptide and Antibodies in the Diabetes Differential
blogs.description: A clinical deep dive into the utility of the glucagon stimulation test and autoantibody screening (GADA, IA-2A, ZnT8). This post explains how to interpret preserved C-peptide levels and negative antibody titers to steer a clinician away from a Type 1 diagnosis and toward genetic screening for MODY.

blogs.title: From 'Novel' to 'Pathogenic': Interpreting Genetic Reports for the Clinician
blogs.description: A guide for non-geneticists on how to handle 'novel' variants found via Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS). Using the case's p.N270S mutation, this post explains the ACMG guidelines, the significance of the DNA-binding domain, and how clinicians can determine if a previously unreported mutation is truly the driver of a patient's disease.
